pairs.difference: A: the station sits dead center and square-on, with solar panels stretched left and right almost to the edges (margin 0.005) and a bright Earth arc filling the bottom. The panels and blue Earth share the station's colours and split attention at thumbnail size, and the magenta-to-blue sky adds a third band. B: the gate sits in a scene, with its walls and path running off the card and the eye led in along the paving. Its 0.157 area is below the real range, but that box covers only the gate leaves, not the brick piers.
pairs.fix: Turn the station to a three-quarter angle and tilt it, drawn larger so it overlaps the planet. Show only a soft, low-contrast curve of planet in one corner, and let one solar panel run off the card edge.

pairs.difference: A: the spyglass runs on a diagonal across a striped background with clear space around it. It is slender, so area 0.168 and height 0.452 fall below the real range, but it still reads at once as a spyglass. B: the ray gun fills the card (area 0.27) and is centered, with the green tip close to the left edge. It also reads instantly. Both are single floating heroes on a plain backdrop with nothing competing, and the composition does not separate them.

A: the whole console sits centered on a hard split of orange wall over grey floor. The grey body merges into the grey floor at thumbnail size, so the lower half loses its edge, and the only thing that stands out is the rows of coloured buttons. B: the plate is tilted and fills the card, with the bright watermelon wedge as one clear focal point against warm wood, and the eye goes there first.
pairs.fix: Remove the grey floor. Place the console tilted on one saturated colour background, drawn larger with its near corner close to the card edge, so its grey body stands out clearly from the background.

pairs.difference: A: the round pod is perfectly frontal and symmetrical, in the exact center, and packed tight into the card (area 0.476, above the real range). Glowing pillars, wall bands and a floor ring all crowd it and compete at thumbnail size, leaving little quiet space. B: the boat lies on a strong diagonal, with the dock cropped by the top-left edges and the water forming a calm field. The hero is clear at once and the framing has direction, like the real plane card.
pairs.fix: Show the pod from a three-quarter angle, slightly off center, and a little smaller. Replace the glowing room with a simple soft backdrop that has no bright rings or light strips near the pod.

pairs.difference: A: the topiary stands as one tall stacked mass on a plain lawn, with a hedge and path receding off the card. Nothing competes with it, and the first read is immediate. B: the ringed planet is centered, with two moons in opposite corners plus stars and pink clouds. Those satellites and the bright cloud streaks scatter the eye at thumbnail size, and the ring runs nearly to both edges (0.937 width).
pairs.fix: Remove the small moons, sparkles and pink cloud streaks. Draw only one large ringed planet, tilted, against a smooth dark starry sky, with one side of the ring slightly cropped by the card edge.

pairs.difference: A: the pool fills the card width in a garden corner, with the duck as a small bright accent in the middle and the fence and grass as quiet context. B: the jacket floats centered on a green burst with even space around it, the same set-up as the real glove card. Both measurements are in the real range, both read at once, and neither shows a framing fault.

A: the ship wheel is frontal and centered with an open margin (0.105, slightly above the real range) on a pale burst and deck. It reads instantly. B: the telescope runs on a diagonal, its slim tripod and thin tube giving a low area (0.163), with the eyepiece thinning out at thumbnail size. Each has one mild outlier, neither fits the generated direction clearly, and the two share the same burst-and-deck framing.

A: the robot stands whole and upright in the middle, with even clearance on all sides and only a small soft shadow, so it looks placed rather than framed. This matches the contained, fully shown generated lesson cards, and at thumbnail size the thin limbs leave the orange showing through. B: the vending machine is a tall solid block at three-quarter view, filling the height with area 0.422 and reading as a single mass.
pairs.fix: Draw the robot larger and closer, turned three-quarter with its body filling more of the card, and let a raised arm or antenna come close to the edge rather than sitting evenly inside the frame.

pairs.difference: A: the open book is cropped by the left and right edges (width 1.0) on a table, with a pot at the right and a railing behind. The white pot draws some attention, but the framing is a cropped scene like the real motel card. B: the folding chair is whole and slightly right of center on a red wall and tan floor, with a thin frame and low area (0.202). Both read clearly and neither departs cleanly from the real framing.

A: the player is tilted and off center to the upper left, with the white cable looping to the lower right. That gives a diagonal path through the card, though the thin cable fades at thumbnail size. B: the saucer sits dead center in the ring target, an evenly contained wide shape (height 0.473, below the real range). It reads instantly but is static, with empty card above and below.
pairs.fix: Bring the saucer closer and tilt it more steeply, so it dives across the card with the dome near the top and the rim nearly reaching both sides, filling more of the height.

pairs.difference: A: the popcorn cart fills the card height (0.869, slightly above the real range) at a three-quarter angle, on blue over paving, and the red and white awning reads first. B: the helmet is a neat centered lump with wide even clearance (margin 0.133, above the real range) on a hard split of green wall over grey floor. The grey floor adds a dull band across the bottom third of the thumbnail, and the white shell and grey floor sit close in value.
pairs.fix: Remove the grey floor and the hard horizon. Draw the helmet larger on one saturated colour background, tilted at a three-quarter angle so it fills most of the card, with its edge close to the card border.

pairs.difference: A: the rocket is tilted upward on a cyan burst, tall in the card with a narrow width (0.556), and has a clear silhouette. B: the submarine lies nearly level on a dark green burst with its propeller and periscope near the edges, and the yellow pops strongly. Both are single floating heroes centered on bursts, as in the real glove card, and both read at once with nothing competing.

pattern: Generated cards stage the object instead of framing it. The whole hero sits centered, often square-on and symmetrical, with even clearance and nothing cropped. Real cards more often bite into the frame or lean on a diagonal, as with the plane, the taxi and the lighthouse cropped at the base. Generated cards also add attention-splitting extras (moons, Earth arcs, glowing room rings) or use a hard colour-wall-over-grey-floor split that dulls the thumbnail and weakens separation. Composition alone is a weak signal on single floating heroes on burst or pattern backgrounds, because real cards use the same set-up.
